The script ran and produced the four outcomes:

```
winner_key=A winner_scale=A pair=(KA, SA)
winner_key=A winner_scale=B pair=(KA, SB)
winner_key=B winner_scale=A pair=(KB, SA)
winner_key=B winner_scale=B pair=(KB, SB)
```

The construction is deliberately per-buffer: the key-only operation selects `K[winner_key]` and the scale-only operation selects `S[winner_scale]`, each from its own independent winner. The resulting pair is a 2-tuple assembled from two separate writes, so no outcome is a single winner "writing the whole pair." The two mixed outcomes, `(KA, SB)` and `(KB, SA)`, are therefore ordinary members of the four-way product set, not contradictions or a single operation straddling both buffers. Everything here is abstract set/tuple bookkeeping over the symbols `KA, KB, SA, SB`; it makes no claim about any hardware or NPU behavior. No files were written and no network or devices were touched — output was stdout only.
